Markets were mixed this morning as optimism about a potential U.S.-Iran deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz wavered as yesterday's tech rally lost steam. Big tech firms, including Apple, Microsoft, and Amazon, all fell.

Artificial intelligence (AI) bellwether Nvidia gained after SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said the firm would use only Nvidia chips, further pressuring AMD. With valuations at record highs, investors are looking for blowout results this earnings season, and AMD — which has a forward P/E ratio of 66 — didn't quite make the mark.

(Updates with index/price moves and company/geopolitical news from the first paragraph.)

US equity indexes traded mixed amid a sharp sell-off in communication services and reports that Iran and Oman have agreed on a proposed shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz, the chokepoint for about a fifth of global oil and natural gas flows.

The Nasdaq Composite fell 0.6% to 26,444.8, and the S&P 500 slipped 0.1% to 7,727.6 after midday Wednesday. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.8% to 54,511.2. Both the S&P 500 and the Dow scaled new peaks for a second straight day earlier in the session.

Communication services, energy and utilities led decliners. Materials and healthcare topped gainers.

Iran said it has reached a deal with Oman on a proposed shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz, a potential step toward a reopening of the waterway for energy supplies, Bloomberg reported Wednesday.

A joint statement from the two countries is in the final drafting stage, Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei was cited as saying Wednesday, Bloomberg reported. Talks between Iran and Oman are "forward-moving," and an agreement would be struck "if certain third parties do not obstruct this process," Baghaei was cited as saying, according to the report.

The front-month US West Texas Intermediate crude oil slipped 0.4% to $75.48 a barrel, and global benchmark North Sea Brent edged up 0.1% to $79.44 a barrel.

SpaceX (SPCX) reported Q2 capital expenditures of $18.37 billion, up from $2.83 billion a year ago, taking the shine off a narrower-than-expected loss and above-consensus revenue growth. Shares slumped 8%, among the worst performers on the Nasdaq.

Shares of Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) dropped 5.5%, one of the steepest decliners on the Nasdaq, after analysts, in a post-earnings conference call late Tuesday, raised questions about the chipmaker's gross margin trajectory. The company reported fiscal Q2 adjusted earnings and revenue above market expectations, and Q3 sales guidance beat consensus.

title: Marvell Stock Amplifies The Market You Already Own
detail:
Marvell Stock Amplifies The Market You Already Own
Trefis Team
Wed, August 5, 2026 at 12:13 PM EDT 3 min read
MRVL
NVDA

QCOM
INTC

Trading disclosure
Photo by manseok_Kim on Pixabay

Its five-year correlation to the index says overlap, and its past-year capture readings say that overlap arrives magnified in both directions.

Marvell Technology (MRVL) stock is up 25% over the last five trading days, against 4.1% for the S&P 500. Runs like that pull money in. But the question that decides your wealth is not where this stock goes next week. It is how much of its return is genuinely its own story, and how much is the market you already own, arriving louder.

Marvell's 0.63 Correlation Is Overlap, Not A Separate Bet

Over the past five years, Marvell has returned 31% a year against the S&P 500's 13.4%, and its correlation to that index over the same window is 0.63, a high reading. A large part of what moves this stock is what moves the index fund you probably already hold. Gold returned 17.2% a year over those same five years, at a correlation to Marvell of 0.13, which is what a genuinely separate return stream looks like. Marvell has been the far better performer, but not the second engine. Since late June it has also been an S&P 500 constituent, so an S&P 500 index fund now owns some of it on your behalf, as do broad technology index funds.

Three Quarters Of Marvell's Revenue Now Rides One End Market

That absence of a separate story has a business explanation. The data center end market contributed 76% of the $2.418 billion Marvell booked in fiscal Q1 2027, sold as interconnect, switching and custom silicon. Management expects interconnect revenue alone to grow more than 70% year over year in fiscal 2027, and says only a handful of companies are driving the AI build-out it supplies. This is not a business cycle of its own; it is a concentrated position on how fast those few buyers keep spending. A return stream resting on one spending cycle is a structure the Trefis High Quality Portfolio deliberately avoids, since it does not depend on the handful of largest technology names to produce its own returns.

Marvell Swings More Than Three Times The Market, In Both Directions

A 0.63 correlation still understates what this stock does to a portfolio. Marvell's annualized volatility over those five years was 64%, against 17.2% for the S&P 500. On days the index rose over the past year, Marvell captured about 356% of the market's gain; on days it fell, it absorbed about 307% of the loss. The tilt is favorable, but the scale is the point: for a year this has been the market's own direction with the volume turned up more than three times each way. The lived version is the past twelve months, in which the stock returned 194% and still sits about 31% below its 52-week high.

title: AMD Shows Strong Outlook, but Warrants Limit Potential, Morgan Stanley Says
detail:
PREMIUM
AMD Shows Strong Outlook, but Warrants Limit Potential, Morgan Stanley Says
MT Newswires
Wed, August 5, 2026 at 12:01 PM EDT 1 min read
AMD
MS

Trading disclosure

Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) is looking "significantly" better in 2027 after Q2 results, but its warrants issuance limits upside potential, Morgan Stanley said in a report Wednesday.

The report said its Q2 results and outlook were modestly above consensus, but below some of the more bullish expectations coming out of its last week's event.

The near-term numbers were not surprising but commentary on 2027 data center revenue of "significantly more than doubling" is positive against Morgan Stanley's 80% estimates, the note said.

"We like the revenue growth but the warrant issuance tempers our enthusiasm," the report said.

The report said the cost of warrants issued to two customers related to the launch of Helios, an open rack-scale AI platform, can't be completely ignored.

The note said the Helios success comes at a marketing expense of issuing over $15 billion in warrants for every $15 billion to $20 billion in revenues for the foreseeable future.

"If that were treated as a cash expense, it would wipe out profitability," the note said.

"To be clear, we aren't objecting to the warrant issuance, but we are saying that it has a negative impact on the earnings of the company over the next 3-4 years, which makes the stock less attractive than peers that aren't doing that," it added.

Morgan Stanley raised its price target to $465 from $410 while keeping its equal weight rating.

title: Can MRVL's Communications Recovery Drive Broad-Based Growth?
detail:
Can MRVL's Communications Recovery Drive Broad-Based Growth?
Subham Roy
Wed, August 5, 2026 at 11:52 AM EDT 3 min read
MRVL
AVGO
AMD
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Marvell Technology's MRVL communications and other business segment has been recovering as customer inventories normalize. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, communications and other revenues increased 29% year over year to $585 million. MRVL's AI data center networking business has been at the center of its growth.

Networking remains a key beneficiary of rising AI cluster size and complexity. Marvell now expects its interconnect business to grow more than 70% year over year in fiscal 2027, supported by scale-out PAM ramp-ups and growing contributions from scale-up and scale-across networking.

Within optics, the company expects TIAs and drivers to exceed a $1 billion annualized run rate in the next few quarters and sees a path to about $1 billion annualized DCI module revenues during fiscal 2028. Management also expects scale-up optics to ramp up in fiscal 2028, with revenues now forecasted to more than double versus its prior outlook of about $150 million.

The company has also launched the Golden Cable initiative to accelerate and expand the Active Electrical Cable (AEC) ecosystem for faster deployment of AI infrastructure by cloud and hyperscaler customers. However, Marvell Technology's move toward lower-margin custom silicon and other AI infrastructure products is resulting in a gradual decline in the gross margin.

However, MRVL expects its communications end market to decline in the mid-single-digit range sequentially in the second quarter while growing in the high-single-digit range year over year, which implies the recovery is continuing but not linear. A steadier baseline outside the data center can moderate volatility through periods when hyperscaler build cycles vary while still keeping the company exposed to long-term infrastructure upgrades.

How Competitors Fare Against MRVL Stock

MRVL faces stiff competition in the AI networking and custom silicon space from Broadcom AVGO and Advanced Micro Devices AMD.

Broadcom is a leader in the domain of custom silicon solutions for data centers. Broadcom's advanced 3.5D XDSiP packaging platform is critical to ensure the performance and efficiency of custom AI XPUs.

Advanced Micro Devices is another established player in the custom silicon solutions and AI accelerator market. Advanced Micro Devices offers semi-custom SoCs and Instinct Accelerators to power data centers.

MRVL's Price Performance, Valuation and Estimates

Shares of Marvell Technology have rallied 157.3% year to date compared with the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry's growth of 35.3%.
